column3: The Hebrew retains the image of putting one’s hand with a wicked person.
The Hebrew refers to “your needy person” and “his lawsuit,” singular.
The Hebrew says “you know the soul of the sojourner,” rather than explaining how it feels to be foreigners.
The Hebrew says “the name of other gods,” singular, and then changes to singular “your mouth.”
The Hebrew repeatedly calls the produce “your works.”
The Hebrew names “the Lord, the LORD,” retaining the divine name alongside the title.
The Hebrew says “your transgressions,” explicitly referring to the addressees.
The Hebrew names the peoples directly without separately adding “the land of.”
The Hebrew names their standing pillars, rather than merely stones.
The Hebrew changes from plural address in “serve” and “your God” to singular “your bread” and “your water.”
The Hebrew preserves the image of giving the enemies’ necks toward you, rather than explicitly saying they run.
